ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: KOFIU Financial Transaction Reports Act requires identification and verification of every beneficial owner of the Yuhan Hoesa before account opening or transaction. The CRO must run daily screening against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU, UK HMT, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs designated persons, and FATF high-risk jurisdictions. All directors, shareholders, signatories, counterparties, and beneficiaries are screened for foreign and domestic PEPs; if any PEP is identified, senior management approval and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth verification are mandatory. Adverse media, criminal record, sanctions-nexus, Interpol, and beneficial-ownership-piercing checks must be documented and retained for at least five years after relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr) and the Commercial Registration Division of the relevant Local District Court, normally the Seoul Central District Court for the main corporate registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean Commercial Act requires the registered company name to be written in Hangul. For a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the form must include the Korean equivalent '유한회사' rendered as 'Yuhan Hoesa' in English. Foreign-language names may be used only as an additional transliterated or translated trade name for cross-border contracts and banking, but the Hangul legal name is controlling. The accepted corporate naming hierarchy has four tiers: Tier 1 distinctive brand or identifier; Tier 2 business-object expression in Korean, e.g., clinical trial contract research organization; Tier 3 liability suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'; Tier 4 registered English transliteration in parentheses for international document purposes. Phonetic transliteration must be sufficiently distinct from any existing registered Korean company name and must avoid misleading ambiguity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 calendar days of a name rejection notification by the Registration Examiner, the applicant must file a written administrative objection with the same District Court Registration Division, relying on Article 254(2) of the Korean Commercial Act, showing the proposed name is distinctive and non-confusable. The Registration Examiner transmits the objection to the district court panel; if rejected again, an appeal to the High Court and thereafter Supreme Court is available under the Administrative Litigation Act. While the appeal is pending, the applicant may simultaneously reserve a new distinctive name through the IROS portal. Each rejected name requires a new filing and prescribed fee; no automatic extension of the original reservation is granted unless an administrative appeal is pending and the court orders preservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or registered-agent-only address is not permissible as the sole registered office of a clinical-trial CRO in South Korea. The Korean Commercial Act and the National Tax Service practice require a physical domestic establishment where the Yuhan Hoesa's directors perform management functions, corporate books and minutes are kept, tax invoices are issued, and regulatory inspectors can visit. For a CRO requiring MFDS authorization under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, the operating office must be capable of supporting clinical-trial record retention, site monitoring, audits, and physical inspections. Korean banks will reject corporate account opening if the address is only a virtual office. A flexible or serviced back-office can be used as a supplementary facility, but cannot replace a real, leased, ecologically verifiable registered office with utility bills, payroll, and business license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The risk of unannounced physical inspection is high for an MFDS-licensed CRO: quantified likelihood 65 to 75 percent within the first 24 months of operation, with an additional targeted inspection upon license renewal and at each clinical-trial protocol amendment. The mandatory compliance checklist includes a physical office lease, company signboard, full-time local employees, outsourced laboratory or archive agreements, clinical-trial records, computerized data systems, audit trails, SOPs, drug accountability records, corporate books, bank statements, NTS tax invoices, payroll filings, insurance policies, and evidence that the site is not a shell or letterbox operation. Registry and municipal tax authorities may also carry out document-based inspections after director changes or address changes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, January 27, 1962, as amended), particularly Articles 543 through 613 governing Yuhan Hoesa and, by reason of Article 560, the applicable stock-corporation provisions of Articles 289, 290, 292, 293, 312, 316, 329, 330, 331, 335, 347, 349, 350, 355, 383, 389, 393, 408, 460, 476, 477, 478, 479, 480, 487, 491, 517, 530-2, 561, 562, 563, 564, 567, 582, 600, 601, 602, 604, 635 and 637; Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, Article 34; Regulation on Safety of Pharmaceuticals, Articles 72 to 76; Korean Good Clinical Practice (KGCP), MFDS Notification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division) and the local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation; Corporation Registration Application; Business Registration Application; MFDS Clinical Trial Plan Approval Application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean Yuhan Hoesa is not subject to a statutory minimum paid-in capital, and the Korean Commercial Act does not require a blocked capital escrow account as a matter of law. In bank practice, however, the subscription proceeds should be deposited into a dedicated pre-incorporation escrow account in the Company's intended name and remain blocked until the court issues the certificate of registration. The Articles of Incorporation must state the exact amount of contribution capital and the number of contribution units, and no capital may be distributed to founders before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

WHEREAS, Yuhan Hoesa (the Company) is a Korean limited liability company to be incorporated under Articles 543 to 613 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and

WHEREAS, the Company's business scope includes contract research organization (CRO) management for multinational drug trials, including clinical trial protocol support, clinical trial site selection and monitoring, data management, biostatistics, regulatory liaison with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), safety reporting, and clinical study report preparation; and

WHEREAS, the Company has received full subscription of its contribution units from its sole founding member; and

WHEREAS, this instrument constitutes the first formal resolution of the board of directors acting with the authority of the initial member in accordance with Article 560 of the Commercial Act.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED as follows:

1. CONTRIBUTION CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The Company's total initial capital is fixed at KRW [CAMOUNT], divided into [CNUMBER] registered contribution units. Each contribution unit has a par value set forth in the Articles of Incorporation. All contribution units have been validly issued and fully subscribed. The subscription funds have been deposited in a blocked escrow bank account opened in the Company's name, and the representative director is instructed to obtain the bank's written confirmation of paid-in contribution and to place that certificate in the corporate records.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The board adopts and ratifies the opening of domestic and foreign currency bank accounts with a branch of a commercial banking institution located in the Republic of Korea. The representative director, together with one additional officer to be named by the representative director, is authorized to sign all checks, wire transfer requests, SWIFT instructions, deposit certificates, and security documents. All milestone invoices and SWIFT payments shall be credited to the Company's operating account.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company is fixed and adopted at the following address in the Republic of Korea: [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS]. All corporate records, notices, process, and governmental correspondence shall be maintained and received at that address. The representative director is authorized to execute or terminate the office lease and to make all filings necessary for relocation if required by business circumstances.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board confirms the following appointments. [NAME] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer. [NAME] is appointed Director and Chief Financial Officer. [NAME] is appointed Corporate Secretary. If a statutory auditor is required under the Commercial Act, an auditor shall be appointed by the members at the next regular general meeting and shall report to the members. Each officer shall hold office until resignation, removal, or successor appointment.

5. REGULATORY AUTHORIZATION AND CRO OPERATIONS. The representative director and any delegate are authorized to prepare and submit a clinical trial plan approval dossier to MFDS, to sign Korean Good Clinical Practice declarations, to execute clinical trial agreements, to appoint institutional review boards, and to engage qualified sub-contractors, all in the name and for the account of the Company.

6. GENERAL AUTHORITY. All actions lawfully taken before this resolution are ratified. Each officer may execute, deliver, or amend any document necessary to implement this resolution and to conduct the Company's business. This resolution shall bind the Company and its successors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) name search and the Civil Notary Public of the competent district in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name preclearance search in the Supreme Court's corporate registration database to confirm that the proposed English and Korean corporate names are not identical to an existing Korean company. Prepare Korean-language Articles of Incorporation that state the company name, the purpose limited to ISIC 7490 clinical trial CRO management and regulatory consulting, the registered office address, the total authorized contribution units, the initial paid-in contribution amount, the name of each founding member, and the number of contribution units subscribed by each member. Have each founding member sign or seal the Articles, appear before a Korean civil notary, and obtain a notarized certificate evidencing the authenticity of the signatures. For foreign founding entities, provide a notarized and apostilled certificate of good standing and any required power of attorney with an attached Korean translation.
required_dossiers: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation signed by each incorporator
Notarization certificate or authentic deed
Passport or corporate identification of each founder
Apostilled certificate of incorporation or good standing for any corporate founder
Power of attorney appointing a local Korean attorney or resident manager
Payment receipt for notary fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry requires a correction, revise and re-sign the Articles, re-notarize the corrected pages, and resubmit. If the name search shows conflict, select a new distinct name and repeat the search before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Subscription and Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking institution in the Republic of Korea selected by the founding member (e.g., a branch licensed under the Banking Act)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before court registration, open a provisional corporate subscription account in the name of the company to be incorporated. Each founding member transmits the agreed contribution amount by wire transfer into this blocked escrow account. No withdrawal shall be made until the court issues the certificate of registration. The bank is requested to issue a certificate of deposit of paid-in capital, stating the depositor identity, the deposit date, and the exact amount. The certificate must match the Articles of Incorporation and the application for incorporation. If subscriber names differ from the founding members, update the subscription ledger and request an amended bank certificate.
required_dossiers: Provisional corporate subscription account application form
Bank transfer receipts for each contribution
Certificate of deposit of paid-in capital
Subscription ledger with unit distribution
Passport or corporate identification of each subscriber
Draft Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains incorrect data, return the certificate to the bank for correction and obtain a replacement before the court filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application at the court's civil registration section after the Articles have been notarized and the capital certificate has been issued. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the certificate of capital deposit, the report on officer appointments, consent forms signed by each director, and the certificate of signature or seal of the representative. Pay the registration tax, the additional local education tax, and the court fee. The court examiner verifies that the company name, purpose, capital, and officers comply with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court enters the company in the commercial register and issues the certificate of registered matters, which is conclusive proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Completed corporation registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit of paid-in capital
Report on appointment of directors and auditor with consent forms
Certificate of seal or signature of the representative director
Power of attorney and foreign apostille documents
Court registration tax and education tax payment receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a supplementation order, the applicant has 14 days to cure. Correct the defective exhibit, pay any shortfall in registration tax, and resubmit. For a rejected name or object clause, the incorporators must approve amended Articles and re-notarize prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Taxpayer Identification at the Local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service of Korea, online via Hometax
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month from the court registration date, apply for corporate business registration on Hometax or at the local tax office. Provide the certified corporate register extract, the Articles, the lease contract, the representative director's identification, and a resolution ratifying the representative's appointment. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate and a corporate taxpayer identification number. This number is used for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding, and foreign-investment reporting. Offices must subsequently register with the local employment insurance and national pension agencies if they hire employees.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate (certificate of registered matters)
Business registration application form
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Lease contract or virtual office consent for the registered office
Identity documents of the representative director
Board resolution adopting the registered office and ratifying officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended due to an address mismatch, obtain a corrected certificate of registered matters from the court, register the exact lease address, and re-file. If the name differs from the tax database, supply the corporate registration certificate with the official Korean name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: MFDS Clinical Trial CRO Regulatory Authorization and KGCP Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Clinical Trials Management Division, via the MFDS online submission portal and Korea Clinical Trials Information (KCTI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each multinational drug trial, submit a clinical trial plan to MFDS and obtain approval before any Korean clinical trial site enrolls subjects. The CRO must ensure the sponsor, trial site, and contract research personnel follow Korean Good Clinical Practice (KGCP) and the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. Prepare a delegated duties matrix, safety reporting procedures, monitoring SOPs, and patient data processing safeguards under the Personal Information Protection Act. Where the CRO stores investigational products, document temperature mapping and restricted access; otherwise, no physical facility license is triggered. Maintain the corporate business registration certificate and MFDS correspondence in the Company's regulatory binder.
required_dossiers: Clinical trial plan approval application
Proof of corporate business registration and court registration certificate
Sponsor delegation agreement in Korean or English
KGCP compliance declaration and SOP manual
Investigational product handling and storage standard form
Institutional Review Board approval or submission record
Personal information processing policy
Clinical trial insurance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS issues a deficiency or rejection, respond within the statutory response window by amending the trial plan; resubmit the corrected dossier and request an expedited review. If approval is denied, pursue an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), Clinical Trials Management Division; for office and employee safety, the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Clinical Trial Plan Approval under Article 34 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act and MFDS Korean Good Clinical Practice (KGCP) recognition; Corporate Business License issued by the Local District Tax Office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - ISIC 7490 clinical trial CRO management is a professional, office-based service; no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If an investigational product depot is later established, an Environmental Registration or site-level review may be required before storage of controlled investigational products.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: 0 kg/day industrial wastewater discharge; 0 kg/day VOC emissions; 0 kg/month hazardous waste generation. General office waste must be handled under the Waste Management Act. Any destruction of investigational product must be documented and handled by a licensed pharmaceutical waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the Civil Defense fire-permit regime at a pure office and CRO facility; however, the Company must obtain the lessor's Completion Certificate of Fire Protection Systems for the leased office and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and employee safety training. If a clinical-trial drug storage room is established, MFDS and KGCP cold-chain temperature monitoring qualifications and local fire-safety inspection for the storage area will be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the electronic portal Home Tax Service (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export customs clearance is administered through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident investor must first incorporate a Korean Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act; the company is then a Korean domestic entity. Tax registration is completed through the National Tax Service. The company or its authorized tax agent must file the electronic business registration application through Home Tax Service within 20 days from the date of commencement of business. The submission pack must include: certified/apostilled formation documents of the foreign investor, articles of incorporation and court registry certificate of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, evidence of the registered business address, power of attorney designating a Korean tax agent, foreign investment declaration certificate under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act when applicable, and any clinical trial service authorization issued by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety if already obtained. The competent district tax office verifies the information and assigns a 10-digit business registration number, which is simultaneously the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT registration number, and issues the business registration certificate. A foreign entity operating directly through a Korean branch rather than a Korean subsidiary must register the branch as a domestic place of business under the same process and must obtain the same business registration number before making taxable supplies in South Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for a pass-through election: South Korea does not have a check-the-box regime, and the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. A wholly-owned domestic parent-subsidiary group may elect the consolidated corporate tax filing system, and hybrid mismatch rules in the International Tax Adjustment Act apply mandatorily rather than by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold: any business maintaining a domestic place of business in South Korea must register for VAT before taxable supplies begin; a Korean corporation is always a general VAT taxpayer, and the simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80,000,000 applies only to individual business owners, not to a Yuhan Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Korean entity must issue electronic tax invoices through NTS Home Tax Service using the official Hometax API or EDI channel. Each e-tax invoice is transmitted to NTS and assigned a unique NTS management number, which acts as the anti-fraud digital stamp and enables the NTS to cross-match buyer and seller invoices in its fiscal clearance system. A corporation cannot use paper tax invoices except for statutory exceptions that do not apply to a corporation. VAT returns are filed semi-annually with a preliminary return for each half-year, due 25 April for January-March and 25 October for July-September, and a final return, due 25 July for January-June and 25 January for July-December; all e-invoice and cash-receipt data must be reconciled to the returns and retained for at least five years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the zero-rating provisions of the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree for physically exported goods, services that qualify as foreign currency earning services supplied to a non-resident business with no Korean domestic place of business, and services physically performed entirely outside South Korea. For a clinical trial CRO, the qualifying supply must be documented contract research services to a non-resident pharmaceutical sponsor, invoiced in foreign currency, with proceeds received through a Korean foreign exchange bank and repatriated into South Korea within the statutory period; the zero-rated exporter must issue a 0% e-tax invoice and maintain the service agreement, protocol, deliverable reports, and foreign currency remittance certificate. If the sponsor has a Korean domestic place of business or the service is invoiced to a Korean resident, the supply is subject to 10% VAT. The zero-rated exporter may apply through Home Tax Service for early refund of attributable input VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic export declaration for any clinical trial materials, biological samples, or equipment physically exported from South Korea; pure service-only CRO zero-rating does not require a customs declaration, but any accompanying goods must be covered by this export declaration.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of trial goods or samples to the foreign destination.
Commercial invoice and packing list with HS codes and clinical trial reference numbers for all exported materials.
Service agreement and clinical trial protocol with the non-resident sponsor identifying the non-resident recipient, scope, and foreign currency payment terms.
Inward foreign currency remittance certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank proving receipt and repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days.
Korean electronic tax invoice issued through Hometax showing the zero rate for the qualifying supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may scrutinize export zero-rating claims through document review, bank confirmation, and exchange of information with the sponsor's tax treaty jurisdiction. Failure to maintain the required contract, e-tax invoice, customs evidence, or foreign currency receipt invalidates the zero rating; the NTS will retroactively assess 10% VAT on the supply, add additional tax up to 40% of the underreported VAT for false or negligent reporting, charge statutory delay interest, claw back any refund already paid, and may refer the case to prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The statutory assessment period is normally five years but extends to ten years where the false zero-rating is intentional concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the sovereign monetary and foreign exchange authority, with supervisory and administrative powers delegated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and licensed foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains an open current-account system, accepting IMF Article VIII convertibility obligations, but retains a reporting-based framework for capital movements. Current-account payments, including clinical-trial service fees, subcontractor invoices, dividend distributions, and interest payments, can be converted at market rates upon presentation of a customs declaration, VAT invoice, contract, or audited resolution. Capital inflows for equity injection into the LLC must first be registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; once a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate is issued, inbound USD is converted to KRW at a domestic foreign-exchange bank using the direct-investment FX purpose code, and the proceeds can be used for business operations. Profit remittances require evidence of payment, tax withholding confirmation, audited financial statements, and no prohibition on the receiving jurisdiction. Outbound payments to foreign CRO sites or laboratories are permissible as invisible trade, subject to contract, shipping or milestone evidence. The Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance may impose temporary capital-flow management measures in crisis scenarios, but the current regime imposes no surrender obligation and no quantitative caps on conversion for legitimate transactions; practical friction is driven by bank-level AML evidence collection rather than by central-bank exchange allocation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, export proceeds must be collected no later than 90 days after the export declaration/loading date unless an extension is approved in advance. The statutory surrender ratio is 0% under the post-1998 liberalization regime; Korean exporters are not required to sell export proceeds to the Bank of Korea. However, the foreign currency received must either be sold to a licensed foreign-exchange bank to obtain KRW at the market rate or be credited to a domestic foreign-currency account in the name of the exporting LLC. The settlement is recorded by the bank in the electronic trade-settlement system for Korea Customs Service verification. A failure to collect within the statutory timeline without prior approval must be reported and may result in administrative fines or loss of trade-settlement facilitation benefits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and effectively not viable as a primary or complementary settlement rail for the Korean LLC. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or other non-bank electronic-money institutions are not licensed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to execute foreign-exchange business for a Korean resident entity. The Act confines foreign-exchange dealing, cross-border transfer and settlement to licensed foreign exchange banks with a Korean banking resolution. An offshore EMI cannot obtain Korea Financial Supervisory Service approval nor use the Korean clearing and reporting channels; attempting to use an EMI to collect sponsor milestone payments or to fund the capital account would fail statutory reporting and expose the LLC to fines. Domestic internet-only banks such as Toss Bank or Kakao Bank could technically onboard the LLC, but they are not universally accepted for FDI Capital Escrow Accounts and are not included in this Tier-1 blueprint.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch appearance is strongly expected for at least one statutory director or authorized corporate signatory when activating the primary account. For non-resident directors, banks typically accept a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney with the corporate director list and business registration, plus a live video interview with the bank's compliance officer. A few banks permit remote KYC if the applicant is referred by a local law firm or certified public accountant, but this is an exception, not the standard. The Yuhan Hoesa should budget for a senior authorized officer to travel to Seoul for the initial account opening, corporate banking token issuance and FX authorization profiling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) chain is layered through foreign holding companies so that the Korean registry extract shows only a corporate shareholder, triggering a 'shell' or 'conduit' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Korean Business Registry extract issued within 30 days, constitutional documents of all intermediate holding companies, an ownership chart from corporate apex to natural persons, passport copies of each UBO with apostille/consular legalization, signed UBO declarations under 25% ultimate ownership thresholds, and an audit trail for all share transfers since incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The clinical-trial milestone wire comes from a third-party payment processor or affiliate not named as payer in the CRO agreement, creating trade-based money-laundering exposure due to undefined commercial basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master clinical trial service agreement, signed protocol and budget with milestone schedule, itemized CRO invoices with unique invoice numbers, bank reference letter from the sponsor's relationship bank confirming the payer's authority, and reconciled wire-level substantiation for each milestone payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No demonstrable local substance is visible on the CRM because the registered address is a virtual office and there is no payroll, lease, or operational data; the bank suspects the Korean LLC is an invoice-relay vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Active commercial lease agreement in the entity name, monthly utilities and telecom invoices, statutory payroll records and 4-pillar Korean social insurance filings for local project staff, principal investigator and coordinator contracts, equipment/IT procurement invoices, and an independent auditor's substance and place-of-management letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media screening hits are triggered from the sponsor, supply-chain counterparties, or the UBO's prior directorships in high-risk jurisdictions; the bank cannot close the risk decision without a corporate-wide sanctions explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Time-stamped screening snapshots from a licensed sanctions/PEP database for all named parties and parent ownership tiers, adverse-media archive with source URLs, anti-corruption and international sanctions representations from the sponsor, and a legal opinion from a qualified Korean or international counsel covering OFAC, EU, UN and Korean FIU clearance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For non-resident shareholders injecting capital into KR_YUHANGHOESA, the first step is to register the planned foreign direct investment with a designated foreign-exchange bank or KOTRA prior to remittance. The investor wires the funds in USD or EUR via SWIFT MT103, paying to the LLC's temporary Capital Escrow Account at a Tier-1 bank such as KB Kookmin or Hana Bank. The MT103 reference must state 'Foreign Direct Investment in KR_YUHANGHOESA', the name of the foreign investor and the pre-notification registration number. The receiving bank will record the inward credit, verify the purpose code for direct investment capital, and then issue the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate / capital verification statement. Only after such certificate is issued may the foreign currency be converted to KRW and transferred into the LLC's basic operational current account. For ongoing clinical-trial sponsor milestone payments, inbound service revenue is treated as current-account receipt and only requires the underlying invoice, contract and bank FX purpose code for service fees; it does not require FDI certification. A standard escrow release condition is that the invested funds remain idle until the bank's capital verification is complete, usually within 30 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound settlement, the LLC should use its Tier-1 domestic bank's corporate e-banking platform with SWIFT MT103 for milestone payments to international sites, subcontractors, and consultancy fees. The bank will require a supporting service agreement, tax invoice/tax invoice type and the beneficial recipient's bank details. For high-value procurement of laboratory equipment, clinical supplies or investigational medicinal products, use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Korean bank to the beneficiary's bank, with transport, insurance and quality documents presented through the documentary credit channel. For smaller or repetitive payments for site recruitment data, use Documentary Collections on D/P or D/A terms with the shipping/certificate package routed through the same relationship bank. The Korean bank will assign a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act clearance code and report the transaction if it exceeds the reporting threshold. To avoid settlement delays, the LLC should pre-file a settlement instruction template and obtain a daily transaction limit in both KRW and USD.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/KRW forward contracts with tenors matched to committed CRO milestone receivables or payables and a bank-approved master agreement.

Cross-currency swap (USD/KRW) only for the purpose of servicing a real foreign-currency borrowing or contractual liability; the notional is capped by the underlying loan principal or committed clinical-trial procurement obligation.

Plain-vanilla FX option collars and European vanilla options on USD/KRW, with the premium paid in KRW and the maximum loss limited to the option premium; a zero-net speculative position must be demonstrable.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for the Korean corporate entity except in exceptional cases involving a non-deliverable cross currency or an approved risk-management purpose; the bank compliance committee must approve the underlying trade documentation before any NDF is booked.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members' meeting of Yuhan Hoesa covering approval of audited or unaudited financial statements, appropriation of profits, and director discharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance act; minutes and financial statements retained at the statutory registered office and presented for inspection if legally demanded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold a valid annual meeting invalidates the financial statement approval; directors and managing members may face civil liability for loss; in an audited entity, failure to present the audit report to the meeting triggers administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Corporations and may support court-compelled dissolution under Commercial Act Article 176 for chronic management failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment on the closed fiscal year's taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea (NTS) via HomeTax or the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by 31 March. A filing extension of up to 1 month is available, making the extended deadline 30 April, with tax payment due by the extended due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax; negligent under-reporting surcharge of 10% of the underpaid amount; fraudulent under-reporting surcharge of 40%; daily delinquency interest of approximately 0.022% per day on unpaid tax. Serious and repeated delinquency leads to forced collection, seizure of bank accounts and receivables, business place closure by the tax office, and administrative strike-off of a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment (local surtax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax collection office of the province, city, county, or district where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of approximately 0.025% per day; non-filing and under-reporting surcharges analogous to national tax penalties up to 20%; prolonged delinquency permits asset seizure and administrative closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit engagement, audited financial statements, and filing of the audit report when compulsory audit thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system; audit report also submitted to the company's members and retained for inspection by NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor must be appointed within 45 days of fiscal year-end; audit report must be completed before the annual members' meeting; the audited financial statements and report must be filed with FSS/DART within 2 weeks after approval by the members' meeting and, in practice, before the corporate tax return deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to submit the audit report is punishable by fines under the Act on External Audit of Corporations, including fines of up to KRW 20 million for omission or false filing; the responsible director and managing member may be subject to criminal referral; the auditor may face disciplinary measures and suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns for the entity's VAT registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary interim returns for January-March and April-June are due by 25 April and 25 October respectively; semi-annual final returns for January-June and July-December are due by 25 July and 25 January of the following year respectively.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted returns attract a 20% non-filing surcharge; negligent under-reporting carries a 10% surcharge, fraudulent under-reporting 40%; unpaid VAT accrues daily delinquency interest at approximately 0.022% per day; repeated non-payment supports seizure and forced closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll withholding reconciliation, wage and tax withholding payment summaries, and employee year-end tax settlement reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Withholding payment summaries for the preceding calendar year must be filed by 10 March; monthly withholding taxes must be remitted by the 10th day of the month following the payment month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete withholding reporting triggers a 20% non-filing surcharge plus daily delinquency interest of approximately 0.022% per day; the company remains secondarily liable for the withheld employee income taxes and may be subject to business place closure if repeated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report where any non-resident shareholder holds equity in the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the designated foreign exchange bank receiving the foreign investment declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any reportable change, including transfer of equity interests, increase or decrease of investment, or change in shareholder details, must be filed within 30 days of the change; no annual report is required if all foreign investment details remain unchanged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a required foreign investment change report within the 30-day window may result in administrative fines of up to KRW 2 million under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and loss of tax or incentive protection for the foreign investment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a private Korean Yuhan Hoesa, mandatory independent CPA audit is triggered under the Act on External Audit of Corporations if, at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, the company's total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). In addition, a company is ineligible for the small-company exemption and therefore subject to mandatory audit if its turnover reaches or exceeds KRW 10 billion or its regular headcount reaches or exceeds 300 employees, even when total assets are below KRW 12 billion. Group-level consolidation tests also apply: if the Yuhan Hoesa is a consolidated subsidiary of any parent already subject to mandatory external audit, the subsidiary must also be audited for Korean statutory reporting purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to entities required to be externally audited under the Act on External Audit of Corporations and to other public-interest entities; non-listed small and medium Yuhan Hoesa entities may prepare financial statements under the Accounting Standards for Non-Public Entities (Korean GAAP / General Accounting Standards of Business Enterprises). Financial statements must be prepared on an accrual basis in Korean won and must apply the same accounting framework consistently from year to year.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a general annual UBO declaration for a private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the company must maintain a current register of members reflecting each equity interest holder, including name, registration number, number of equity interests, amount paid, and date of acquisition. Any transfer of equity interests in a Yuhan Hoesa requires member consent under the Korean Commercial Act unless the articles of incorporation provide otherwise, and the resulting change must be recorded in the statutory registers and reported to the competent registration court within 14 days. Where a foreign investor holds equity, any transfer or change in foreign shareholding must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days of the triggering event. The statutory registers must be available at the registered office for member inspection, pledgee inspection, and lawful court order.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 40,000 (applicable only when statutory audit thresholds are triggered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national CIT headline for tax base exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local surtax resulting in 26.4% aggregate top marginal rate; lower statutory progressive brackets are 9% (up to KRW 200 million), 19% (from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion), and 21% (from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act for qualifying CRO clinical research, up to 25% of qualifying expenditures plus additional credits for new-growth-engine technologies; 50% income tax reduction for 5 years for technology transfer of patented clinical-trial inventions; free economic zone and foreign investment zone corporate income tax holidays of 50% to 100% for 3 to 7 years; no standalone patent box regime but CRO research credits materially reduce the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement with attached detailed schedules and the Report of International Transactions, filed electronically through the Korean National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the entity is also subject to semi-annual interim corporate tax prepayments for fiscal years longer than six months, but those are prepayments and not a separate return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the Korean fiscal year; with HomeTax e-filing, the filing period is automatically extended one month, and a one-month further extension is available to small and medium enterprises. A December year-end CRO must therefore file by March 31, or April 30 with the e-filing extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter company registration number, legal name, business address, fiscal year start and end date, ISIC 7490 code, and entity type. Disclose the direct and indirect foreign shareholding percentage of every non-resident shareholder and identify the domestic withholding agent responsible for dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax per the Korean statutory income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Korean GAAP or K-IFRS net income before tax. For CRO milestone revenues, recognize income when the contractual milestone is objectively performed and collection is probable; include milestone wires received from foreign sponsors in gross turnover; remove any intercompany revenue that has no substance or cannot be supported by a valid CRO service contract.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment to accounting income: non-taxable income, nondeductible expenses, temporary differences, and tax reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back nondeductible corporate expenses including excess entertainment expenses, penalties, fines, bribes, and donations over statutory ceilings; subtract tax-exempt income; apply timing differences for provisions and impairment. For cross-border CRO service charges, any royalty, management fee, or service fee paid to a foreign affiliate is deductible only if the amount is at arm's length and withholding certificates for the non-resident recipient are filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International transaction adjustment line under the International Tax Adjustment Act
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Yuhan Hoesa has controlled cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, compute the arm's length price and adjust taxable income accordingly. Common adjustments for CROs include benchmarking clinical trial service fees, data-management charges, investigator recruitment fees, and overhead recharges against comparable uncontrolled transactions. A failure to make this adjustment is a primary non-resident tax red flag.

Apply the statutory loss carryforward of 10 years for domestic corporations to offset taxable income. Losses of the domestic Korean company cannot be transferred to or used by non-resident shareholders, and losses from a foreign permanent establishment are not deductible unless specifically recognized under the treaty and domestic laws.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation at progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% national corporate tax brackets to the retained tax base, then compute the 10% local corporate income tax surcharge on the national tax. For a multinational CRO, the effective rate is not reduced by foreign shareholder presence; the entity is taxed at the domestic Korean entity-level rate on worldwide income, subject to foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits, and treaty-exempt income provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim R&D tax credits for qualifying clinical trial development expenditures, foreign tax credits for withholding taxes paid on overseas service income, and withholding credits for Korean-source payments received by the company. Attach the relevant tax credit schedules and preserve TRC documents for any treaty-reduced rate applied to inbound payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable, interim prepayments, and withholding liabilities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset the computed tax against interim prepayments and show the remaining balance. Separately state dividend WHT liabilities on any distribution made to non-resident shareholders, royalty WHT on foreign licensor payments, and interest WHT on intercompany loans; remit those withholdings by the 10th day of the month following the payment month. Failure to declare dividend WHT in the annual filing exposes the director personally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory attached schedules and international transaction disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Report of International Transactions, transfer pricing Local File and Master File where the statutory thresholds are met, country-by-country reporting notification if applicable, foreign bank account reports, and the schedule of non-resident shareholder distributions. The return is not complete unless all cross-border related-party transactions are disclosed with supporting intercompany agreements, benchmark studies, and substance documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid final corporate tax, subject to a minimum penalty; unfaithful or false returns trigger a 10% understatement penalty or a 40% fraudulent misstatement penalty respectively. Late payment interest accrues daily at the statutory rate published by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, currently around 0.022% per day or approximately 8% per annum. Willful tax evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million; delinquent taxpayers with unpaid tax above KRW 500 million may be blacklisted, publicly identified, denied tax clearance certificates, and restricted from leaving Korea.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22.0% aggregate (20% national withholding rate for non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surtax, which is 10% of the 20% national tax). For Korean resident individual shareholders the statutory dividend withholding environment is different, but the outbound non-resident dividend repatriation rate applicable to Yuhan Hoesa is 22% in the absence of treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim any Korea double tax treaty relief, the foreign shareholder and the Korean payer must submit an Application for Reduction or Exemption of Withholding Tax through HomeTax or the competent district tax office before payment, or file a refund claim within 3 years if withholding was applied at the statutory rate. The mandatory package includes a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty country tax authority, a Beneficial Ownership Certificate confirming that the recipient is not a conduit or nominee agent, evidence of the applicable shareholding threshold and minimum holding period, the dividend resolution, and a substance declaration identifying the core income-generating activities. The Korean tax authority will apply the principal purpose test and deny relief if obtaining treaty benefits was a main purpose of the arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalty payments to non-resident payees are subject to the same statutory 20% national withholding rate plus 2% local surtax, yielding an aggregate 22% rate. Under most Korean double tax treaties the reduced rate for interest and royalties is 10%, while dividend treaty rates range from 5% for substantial corporate shareholders to 15% for portfolio investors. Royalties for the use or right to use clinical-trial protocols, know-how, patents, and data are eligible for the reduced rate only if the non-resident is the beneficial owner and there is no back-to-back
